A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same SpikingBrain study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and end matter support reliable comparison. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark evaluations, GPU and CPU inference measurements, MetaX training performance, and spiking-scheme analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-6 and the efficiency, spike-distribution and firing-map figures.

M1.justification: The hybrid architectures, MoE upcycling, adaptive-threshold rule and coding schemes are retained. The added gradient-handling and bitwise-coding explanations do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets, language coverage, downstream tasks, and GPU/CPU test scenarios are unchanged. The training-data description moves from v1 Section 3.2 to v2 Section 3.4; the new platform diagram summarizes existing deployment coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Falcon-Mamba, Mistral, Zamba-v1, Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5. Comparator membership also matches within Tables 2-5 and the CPU comparison against Llama3.2-1B.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 8k/32k/128k continual-pretraining stages, approximately 150B-token budget, SFT sample counts, evaluation metrics, frameworks and hardware configurations. No new or revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 retains the same before/after-spiking accuracy comparison, spike-distribution analysis, coding-strategy firing maps and energy estimates. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 4 still reports H100 TTFT measurements averaged over 10 runs. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, with no added seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All six tables and matched result plots retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 4 retains TTFT values of 1054 ms at 1M tokens and 1073 ms at 4M; the 4M Qwen2.5 comparison remains extrapolated.

T1.justification: v2 adds Eq. (28), supplying explicit 2^(t-1) weighting for bidirectional bitwise reconstruction and its matrix-projection identity beyond v1's generic unweighted spike-sum formula. The remaining mathematics is retained; displaying the existing gating identity as Eq. (12) is only a presentation change.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about the models, conversion efficiency, TTFT speedups, sparsity and MetaX feasibility. The expanded platform summary reiterates deployment capabilities and neuromorphic potential already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.3.2 newly states that unsigned binary coding is inapplicable to adaptive-threshold spiking. Section 2.2 also expands the rationale for the architecture trade-offs, discussing parallelism simplicity and additional attention parameters and FLOPs.

D1.justification: Section 3.3.1 newly explains that spike-generation gradients can be bypassed using straight-through estimation. This adds implementation guidance without establishing an implementation change. Calibration, quantization, hardware and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 92 works and retain their research positioning. References 10-14 are reordered following changes to the contribution-bullet order, without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, adjusts author information, expands explanatory passages and reorganizes Section 3, separating MoE upcycling from the relocated multi-stage pipeline. Acknowledgements and author-contribution statements are added; the overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds platform-compatibility Figure 2 and redraws the spike-coding schematic, now Figure 4, with dendrite, time-index and reset annotations. Existing result displays are retained and reflowed, including moving Table 5 alongside the GPU-efficiency discussion.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies previously underspecified gradient handling and bitwise projection weighting, making the spiking procedure easier to understand and reproduce. The binary-coding qualification and revised diagrams also improve clarity. These are useful but limited gains; the experimental evidence and central claims remain unchanged.
